nodes.name: Wet-season rains
nodes.desc: Seasonal rain drives growth of grasses and forest plants on the hills and in the valleys of the reserve.

nodes.name: Dry-season fire
nodes.desc: Savanna woodland and hilltop grassland in this region burn in the dry season, which renews grass growth and clears dead material.

nodes.name: Streams & gallery forest
nodes.desc: Strips of forest along watercourses hold moisture through the dry season and shelter plants and animals that need damp ground.

nodes.name: Soil & nutrients
nodes.desc: Soil in the hills and valleys holds the nutrients and moisture that plants draw on.

nodes.name: Fungi, termites & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Bluestem grasses
nodes.desc: Tall tropical grasses of the savanna. Hyparrhenia is among the grasses kob are known to favour.

nodes.name: Trema
nodes.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree recorded near the reserve, found in forest edges and clearings where it makes small fruits.

nodes.name: Kanya
nodes.desc: A tree of damp forest and stream edges in West Africa, recorded near the reserve; it bears large fruits and is valued for its seed fat.

nodes.name: Termites
nodes.desc: Fungus-growing termites that collect plant litter and build mounds. They are a major food for reptiles, birds and other insect-eaters.

nodes.name: Buffon's kob
nodes.desc: A grazing antelope that favours short grass near water. Aerial surveys in the 1980s counted it as the most numerous antelope in the reserve.

nodes.name: Roan antelope
nodes.desc: A large grass-eating antelope of woodland and savanna; the western subspecies ranges from Senegal to Benin.

nodes.name: African elephant
nodes.desc: Eats grass, browse and fruit and can reshape woodland. Poaching in the 1990s left only a remnant population in the reserve.

nodes.name: Straw-coloured fruit bat
nodes.desc: Feeds on fruit, flowers and leaves and spreads seeds through forests. Recorded near the reserve.

nodes.name: Common bulbul
nodes.desc: A widespread songbird that eats fruit and insects. A GloBI record shows black kites taking it.

nodes.name: African pied hornbill
nodes.desc: A forest hornbill, the most recorded bird near the reserve, that eats fruit and insects.

nodes.name: Common agama
nodes.desc: A sun-loving lizard that eats mainly ants, grasshoppers, beetles and termites. Males hold territories around trees or rocks.

nodes.name: African harrier-hawk
nodes.desc: A raptor with double-jointed legs that raids cavity nests for eggs and chicks and also hunts reptiles and insects.

nodes.name: Black kite
nodes.desc: An opportunistic hunter and scavenger. GloBI records show it taking straw-coloured fruit bats and common bulbuls.

nodes.name: Palm-nut vulture
nodes.desc: An unusual vulture that mostly eats fruit but also takes frogs, insects, small animals and carrion.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: A generalist cat that takes medium-sized antelope where they are common. It has become rare across West Africa, so its local status is uncertain.
